newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Empire East denies bankruptcy rumours.
newsitem.headline: Empire East denies bankruptcy rumours.

text.p: Philippine house builder Empire East Land Holdings Inc on Tuesday denied rumours in the stockmarket that it was about to declare bankruptcy.

"We categorically and vehemently deny the rumours circulated in the stock exchanges today alleging that Empire East has declared, or is about to declare, bankruptcy," corporate secretary Enrique Santos Sy said in a letter to the Philippine Stock Exchange.
"...Contrary to such speculation, the company is in fact in a very sound financial condition," Sy said in his letter, a copy of which was furnished to reporters.

Heavy selling in the stocks of Empire East and its parent Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc on Tuesday pulled down the Philippine Stock Exchange's main stock index by 2.87 percent, or 84.53 points, to 2,860.45.
Empire East ended down by 29.81 percent, or by 1.55 pesos, at 3.65 while its Megaworld dropped 29.25 percent, or 1.55 pesos to 3.75.
The firm has asked the exchange to take appropriate steps to put a stop to the "malicious rumour-mongering which endangers not only our company but the entire economy."

"Such vicious and unfounded rumours are a clear attempt on the part of some unscrupulous parties to undermine not only the integrity of the company but also investors' confidence in Empire East's shares," Sy said.
